questions.stem: Suppose fresh alfalfa contains $$ 60\% $$ dry matter content. If a farmer provides $$ 10\text{ kg} $$ of fresh alfalfa to the cow daily, how much moisture content in kilo gram is the cow obtaining from the fresh alfalfa per day?
explanation_steps:
**Step 1:** Calculate Moisture Percentage.
$$ \text{Moisture } \% = 100\% - \text{Dry Matter } \% = 100\% - 60\% = 40\% $$

**Step 2:** Calculate Moisture Weight.
$$ \text{Moisture Weight} = \text{Total Fresh Weight} \times \text{Moisture } \% $$
$$ \text{Moisture Weight} = 10\text{ kg} \times 0.40 = 4\text{ kg} $$

similar_questions.stem: Suppose fresh alfalfa contains 70% moisture (water). If a farmer provides 5 kg of fresh alfalfa to the cow daily, how much **dry matter** content in kg per day is the cow obtaining from the alfalfa?
explanation_steps:
**Step 1:** Calculate the percentage of Dry Matter (DM).
$$ DM\% = 100\% - Moisture\% = 100\% - 70\% = 30\% $$

**Step 2:** Calculate the weight of the Dry Matter in the 5 kg sample.
$$ DM \text{ weight} = Total \text{ weight} \times DM\% $$
$$ DM \text{ weight} = 5 \text{ kg} \times 0.30 = 1.5 \text{ kg} $$

Result: 1.5 kg.
